why: Nested k[...] groups are decoded with a stack of saved contexts: '[' pushes (text so far, repeat count) and starts fresh, ']' pops it and appends the inner text repeated. It is matching pairs where each stack entry carries extra data (the count and the outer text), the parsing form of a stack.
hints: When you reach ']', what do you need to know to finish this group?
The text decoded inside the group, the repeat count written before its '[', and the text that came before that count. The innermost open group is the one closing, so keep them on a stack.
Scan once: accumulate digits into num; on '[' push (current text, num) and reset both; on ']' pop (prev, k) and set current = prev + current * k; letters append to current.
pitfalls: Repeat counts can have several digits ("12[a]"): build the number digit by digit.
Plain letters after a group ("2[ab]cd") belong to the outer text, not to the group.
